title: A systematic comparison of Large Language Models for automated assignment assessment in programming education: Exploring the importance of architecture and vendor

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing the distribution of awarded points, mean scores, and variance across 18 different Large Language Models on over 6,000 student programming submissions to identify systematic tendencies toward grading strictness or leniency (e.g., 'liberal' vs. 'restrictive' grading philosophies) compared to human teachers and model consensus.
